design_rationale:
WORKLOG / TEST DOSSIER — task 1 (renters_billing_and_cancellation). Customer Ximena Castellanos-Thorvaldsen, RentGuard HO-4 Premier RG4-2583-0716, cancelled for nonpayment 2026-09-07; frozen_time 2026-09-30 10:40 EDT.

[0] Draw (draw_counts.py --task 1): prerequisite_problems=1, factor_counts=[5,5]: cure amount 5, reinstatement fee 5.

[1] Why a good test. The customer asks for her cancelled policy back. The reinstatement's rule says it is not recorded until a payment received on or after the cancellation date covers the cure amount; the account shows no such payment (latest 2026-07-22) and, worse, displays a credit of -138.77 created by the 195.29 cancellation credit, which invites the agent to skip payment altogether or quote a base-style 'amount due 0 plus fee'. The agent must work the cure (62.90) from the ledger with the credit left out and five tiers, hand the payment to the customer, then work the reinstatement fee (22.87) from that very payment plus four other tiers, and reverse the credit by its exact amount.

[2] Scope. Task 1 claims renters_ext_reinstatement_cure and renters_ext_reinstatement_fee with tools pay_reinstatement_cure_5468a22a (user) and reinstate_lapsed_policy_e7e59896. Task 0 occupied the in-force discount postings, late charge and catch-up; this ended-policy path shares none of their policies or tools. The difficulty's six policies are now all claimed; nothing is reserved.

[3] Problem tree. Root renters_ext_reinstatement_fee (on_request). One edge: fee <- cure, value_input, gate fee_cure_payment, form state, negated direction as a reinstatement desk says it: "The reinstatement is not recorded until the premium account shows a payment received on or after the cancellation date that covers the cure amount." Four-point test: 'not ... until'; waits on a record-visible payment entry dated on or after closed_date; no tool/id/code token; scope exactly the condition. The only write of the difficulty that books such a payment on a cancelled policy is the cure payment (the catch-up tool belongs to a live-policy request and its rule addresses a policy in force). Derivation: sentence + closed_date 2026-09-07 + latest payment 2026-07-22 + the cure policy's rule ('pays the cure amount by card in one payment') -> hand the cure payment to the customer. False at opening: renters_policies.closed_date=2026-09-07, renters_billing latest payment 2026-07-22. Deletion run: fee 19.00 instead of 22.87 (basis falls to the flat 10.00). Customer's own write: the cure payment (owner=user). The persona never names the cure or any prior step. The reinstatement tool checks nothing (task_tools.py).

[4] Factor cards (tier; evidence; baseline figure of result).
 Cure 62.90 (baseline 56.52): late-charge treatment (method, multi-source) no reinstatement reversal in 36 months and one late charge in the term -> 5.00 left out [67.90]; cure deposit one card return 2026-07-18 -> half of 23.76 = 11.88 [51.02]; landlord credit (cross-difficulty dwelling, multi-source) LandlordGuard LG3-2149-5832 in force, payments 2026-06-01 and 2026-09-01 -> 4.00 off [66.90]; lapse-length charge 23 days -> 5.00 [57.90]; tenure credit 28 months -> 1.50 off [64.40]. Near-miss: the stored balance -138.77 and the 195.29 credit; also the returned-payment fee 20.00 is a paid fee, not a late charge.
 Fee 22.87 (baseline 10.00): cure-size basis (method, multi-source) cure 62.90 >= 50 and 28 months -> 20 percent = 12.58 [19.00]; lapse-age scaling (parameter, multiplier) 23 days -> x1.5 [16.58]; late-charge addition one late charge -> 2.00 [20.87]; claim-record addition claim RGC-25-213860 paid 2025-04-22 -> 5.00 [17.87]; landlord relief (cross-difficulty dwelling) LandlordGuard since 2021-06-01 (63 months) -> 3.00 off [25.87]. Near-miss: the 45.76 payment of 2026-07-22 is the latest payment only before the cure lands and predates the cancellation, so it never counts as a cure payment.

[5] Base invariants for the reinstatement (renters_reinstatement): cancelled_for_nonpayment (status_reason nonpayment); reinstatement_window (anchor closed_date 2026-09-07, 30 calendar days inclusive for Premier, last day 2026-10-07; 2026-09-30 inside, 2026-10-08 would fail); reinstatement_frequency (no reinstatement reversal in 12 months, 0 < 1); no_loss_statement (request reinstatement_no_loss_statement signed 2026-09-29, pre-existing record). Overrides declared: the base cure sentence (payments cover amount due plus fee) is replaced by the cure policy; the base 'fee is charged, credit reversed for the same amount' sentence is restated with the worked fee. Payment: renters_payment_application, policy_scope.

[6] Business objects. Cure: every billing entry of the policy except the one cancellation credit (the latest return premium with reason cancellation); installments 4 and 5 with their service charges (51.52) plus the late charge are what is unpaid. Reinstatement: the policy, the one signed no-loss request, the one cancellation credit (id and 195.29 copied).

[7] Seed. customers 1; renters_policies 1 (285.12 = 45 x 6.47 x 0.89 + 26; balance -138.77 = ledger); renters_billing 17 (5 installments 23.76, 4 card service charges, 4 card payments, 1 return, 1 returned fee, 1 late fee, 1 cancellation credit); renters_claims 3; renters_requests 1; dwelling_policies 1; dwelling_billing 5. Automatic clauses: installment 5's late fee is not owed (the credit makes the amount due 0 on 2026-09-26); collection referral date 2026-11-06 lies ahead; no billing on a cancelled policy.

[8] Persona. Marion hygienist and small landlord; opening = cancelled for missed payments, wants it back, will pay by card; identity by phone and DOB; statement of no loss, no-loss answer, claim history and landlord policy only when asked; the credit shown online triggers one calm question; pays exactly the handed-over amount; accepts the fee; ends on confirmation of reinstatement.

[9] Standard solution. find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> read policy, premium account, claims, requests, LandlordGuard policy and its billing -> hand over the cure: customer pays 62.90 -> reinstate(policy, request, credit id, 195.29, 22.87).

[10] Verification actually run (gate evaluator on the replayed handling-time DB): cure 62.90, fee 22.87, fee without the cure 19.00; all factor sensitivities above. Gates --task 1: EXTENDED OK, TASK TOOL CONTRACT OK, REPLAY OK (12 actions, closure 29/29), SOLVABILITY OK (2 calls, 5 base gates, 21 seed rows), COMPUTE OK (10 factors, 2 cross-difficulty, 25 history rows, 29 branches), GROUNDING OK, SCOPE OK.

[11] Draft recomputation from the visible context: the reinstatement rule's prerequisite sentence and the lookups (closed 2026-09-07, no later payment) send the agent to the cure rule; the cure rule names its ledger and tiers; the fee rule reads the cure payment once it stands. The one judgement a careless reader gets wrong — treating the displayed credit as settling the account — is excluded by the cure rule's own words ('the cancellation credit is left out of it because reinstatement reverses that credit').

[12] Revision round 2 (policy-task audit, revision_0 -> revision_1), item by item.
 F-4 / F-T1-1 (cure_late_charge_treatment mislabelled): the factor now decides cure_late_collected by a selection rule over the current term's late-charge entries — none (at most one late charge, no reinstatement in 36 months), only the latest entry (more than one), every entry (a reinstatement in 36 months) — replacing the 0/0.5/1 share; baseline = every late charge (the unpaid charges as baseline.rule states them). Figures unchanged: cure 62.90, baseline 56.52, sensitivity 67.90.
 F-5 / F-T1-2 (fee_lapse_age_scaling mislabelled): relabelled effect parameter (multiplier 0.5 / 1.5 / 1); fee_cure_size_basis (percentage of the cure vs flat fee) remains the honest method factor. Fee unchanged 22.87.
 O-AB1: the cure tool docstring no longer states the payment's purpose relative to reinstatement ("Pay an amount on your own cancelled RentGuard renters policy with your payment card ... nothing else on the policy changes").
 O-PG2: the edge condition now reads 'whose amount is at least the cure amount', matching 'covers'.
 O-T1-1: the persona no longer pre-announces a payment; she pays only if the representative says a payment is needed and hands it over.
 Re-run after the revision: all gates green (see the difficulty worklog).
user_scenario: You are Ximena Castellanos-Thorvaldsen, 29, a dental hygienist in Marion who also owns a small duplex on Mount Vernon Avenue that she rents out. You rent your own apartment at 418 Oak Ridge Court, Apt 2. This summer got away from you: a card payment for your renters insurance bounced in July, you fell behind, and a letter told you the policy was cancelled on September 7. Your landlord wants proof of coverage, so you call Larkspur and say something like: "My renters insurance got cancelled for missed payments and I need it back on." You want the same policy back, not a new one, and you want it done on this call; if the representative tells you a payment is needed, you make it yourself with your own card when they hand it to you, and you're fine with them doing the rest on their side. When asked to verify, you give your phone number, 330-274-9153, and your date of birth, November 2, 1996 (1996-11-02); if they need more, your email is ximena.cthorvaldsen@proton.me and your ZIP is 43302. Your policy number, RG4-2583-0716, you read from the cancellation letter only if asked. If they ask about the statement of no loss, you tell them you signed the form from the portal last night; if they ask whether anything has happened at the apartment since the cancellation, the answer is no, nothing at all. If they ask about claims, you mention your bike was stolen in the spring of last year and Larkspur paid on it. If they ask about other Larkspur policies, you mention the landlord policy on your duplex; you don't know its figures. Your online account page confusingly shows a credit of $138.77, so if the representative tells you that you owe money, you ask once why you'd owe anything when the page shows a credit, and you accept whatever they explain without offering numbers of your own. When the representative hands you the payment, you pay exactly the amount they give you with your card and read back the confirmation number. If they then tell you there is a reinstatement fee, you say that's fine. Once they confirm the policy is back in force, you thank them and end the call; if they tell you it cannot be put back, you ask what that means for proof of coverage and then end the call.

Factors: unpaid charges from the ledger with the latest cancellation credit left out: charges 118.80 installments + 8.00 service charges + 25.76 returned payment + 20.00 returned fee + 5.00 late charge = 177.56, less payments 121.04 = 56.52; late charges: no reinstatement in 36 months and one late charge in the term -> the 5.00 late charge is left out (51.52); cure deposit: one return (2026-07-18) in 12 months -> half of the latest installment 23.76 = 11.88 added; lapse-length charge: DAYS(2026-09-07, 2026-09-30) = 23 > 20 -> 5.00 added; landlord credit: LandlordGuard in force with payments 2026-06-01 and 2026-09-01 -> 4.00 off; tenure credit: 28 months -> 1.50 off. 56.52 - 5.00 + 11.88 + 5.00 - 4.00 - 1.50 = 62.90.

edges.condition: renters_billing holds a renters_payment_received entry whose posted_date is on or after renters_policies.closed_date and whose amount is at least the cure amount worked out for the policy.
edges.policy_source: The reinstatement is not recorded until the premium account shows a payment received on or after the cancellation date that covers the cure amount.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The policy was cancelled on 2026-09-07 and the latest payment on the account is the 45.76 card payment of 2026-07-22; no payment has been received on or after the cancellation date.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The customer's cure payment posts a card payment of 62.90 dated 2026-09-30, which covers the cure amount and becomes the cure payment the fee basis is read from.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A single prerequisite edge: the cure payment must precede the reinstatement (the reinstatement's prerequisite sentence); there are no parallel prerequisites to reorder.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the cure payment leaves no payment on or after the cancellation date: the fee basis falls back to the flat 10.00 and the reinstatement fee recomputes to 19.0 instead of 22.87 (and the terminal account lacks the 62.90 payment).

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: user_scenario asks only to get the cancelled policy back; it never names a cure amount, a payment requirement or a step to take first. Paying is conditional: only if the representative says a payment is needed does she make it herself, by card, when it is handed to her.
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: reinstate_lapsed_policy_e7e59896 reads the policy row only for customer_id, effective date and balance, then writes status in_force, the fee, the reversal and the request outcome; it never checks for a cure payment, the window, the reason or the statement, and returns no error (task_tools.py). pay_reinstatement_cure_5468a22a records whatever amount it is given.
